prerequisites: Record CursorHide hide-after-inactivity setting and start PowerToys non-elevated.
reproduce.expected: Pointer visibility restores on activity across privilege boundaries; disabling/exiting never strands the system cursor.
steps: Enable hide-after-inactivity and verify restoration over a normal application.
Open elevated Task Manager, wait past the hide delay and move/click; repeat with always-on-top off and on.
Switch to elevated CMD and move/click, then a normal app. Record visible cursor separately from working input.
Repeat with elevated PowerToys as a control, then disable CursorHide and verify cleanup.

fix_assessment.rationale: A real reproducible visibility failure warrants focused investigation; the specific hook/state/restore mechanism is not yet demonstrated.

known_information: Original report supplies0.102.2933, non-elevated operation, a diagnostic ZIP and a Task Manager reproduction.

Current AutoHideCursorWorker routes low-level mouse activity into State.OnMouseInput and restores via the cursor hider. Source inspection does not prove which stage fails on the reported release.

verification: Non-elevated PowerToys with normal versus elevated foreground apps, and elevated PowerToys control.
After hide delay, mouse movement restores visible cursor while input remains functional; switching between two elevated apps must not strand it.
Disable CursorHide and exit PowerToys to verify restoration; do not alter secure-desktop policy.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: elevated foreground interaction interrupts activity observation or cursor restoration while the worker remains non-elevated. The exact failing stage is not established by the current reports.
proposed_fixes.title: Isolate privilege-dependent CursorHide restore failure
